How to Train Your Dragon is such a nostalgic movie! Watching it as an adult took me back to my childhood summers spent lazing around, watching one movie after the other. I love this movie because it reminds you that taking the unconventional path might be slightly harder, but it is far more rewarding in the end. It also reminds you that you never have to be alone and that there will always be people to support you. No matter how crazy your idea is, you have to find the right people. The unique relationship between Hiccup and Toothless pulls you in, making you wish that you had your own pet dragon. Overall, the movie is sweet and a must-watch for anyone looking to spend a cosy Sunday afternoon reminiscing your childhood.

I almost got choked up by the score of this film. The animation looks insane for 2010, and the film is such a phenomenal misfit story. A lot of DreamWorks films kind of sit on that central theme. One of the very few examples where there is a different adaptation that adapts hardly anything from the books and is still good. I think an adaptation is, in the end, an adaptation, not a recreation of the source material that already exists. Love this film, and I will revisit it hopefully soon.

I will forever love this movie; it's just so good and easily one of the best animated movies I've seen. The animation, the story, the characters, everything about this movie is beautiful. It’s such an enjoyable film, and getting to watch dragons will always be fascinating to me. I adore Hiccup and Toothless's bond; it is so pure and one of the most beautiful, unique friendships in cinema. It serves as a perfect example of the movie's most important theme: tearing down prejudice. I found it so brilliant how the story uses humans and dragons to teach us that we shouldn't let prejudice or fear dictate our perspective of others who seem different from us. Getting to watch Hiccup and Toothless's friendship slowly grow and get stronger is absolutely fantastic. We see Hiccup genuinely getting curious about Toothless, beginning to study him and get to know him from a more empathetic and understanding perspective, instead of just seeing him as something to kill like the other Vikings do. I love that it's a very universal message that we can all learn from, kids and adults alike. The soundtrack is a must-mention when talking about this movie because it is just so good. It's one of my favorites, and the track "Test Drive" always gives me chills when I listen to it. Of course, the sequence itself is also amazing to watch, but the soundtrack definitely elevates it to being truly epic and iconic. Toothless is just so cute and awesome, really mades wish to ride a dragon This movie made me love dragons, and it will forever hold a special place in my heart. “I wouldn’t kill him, because he looked as frightened as I was.
